data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

extract_result.subject: Litigation Retention Policy for Documentary Materials including Electronically Stored Information
extract_result.scope: The retention policy set forth herein applies to all employees and contractors of the USDA and applies to all documentary materials, including record and non-record ESI made, sent, or received in the transaction of USDA business.
extract_result.purpose:
Both record and non-record documentary materials in paper or electronic format frequently become the subject of litigation. Employees create and maintain an increasing portion of business information using computers. This electronically stored information (“ESI”) must be managed alongside traditional paper records to ensure compliance with Federal laws and records management regulations. While not all papers or ESI are agency records, they may nevertheless be relevant evidence subject to discovery that is compelled or sanctioned by a court or administrative tribunal in litigation. Unmanaged and unidentified ESI residing on USDA computers also poses a threat to the Department's ability to document and reconstruct business and decision-making processes.

The purpose of this policy is to prescribe Departmentwide enterprise policies and responsibilities related to the retention of record and non-record documentary materials, including ESI, for discovery or other litigation-related purposes.

policy_statements.source_text: The retention policy set forth herein applies to all employees and contractors of the USDA and applies to all documentary materials, including record and non-record ESI made, sent, or received in the transaction of USDA business.
policy_statements.target: all employees and contractors of the USDA

policy_statements.source_text: Discovery: Discovery is the process of identifying, locating, securing and producing evidence, including testimony, things, information, and materials for utilization in the legal process.

The term is also used to describe the process of reviewing all materials which may be potentially relevant to the issues at hand and/or which may need to be disclosed to other parties, and of evaluating evidence to prove or disprove facts, theories or allegations.
There are several formalized methods of conducting discovery, the most common of which are interrogatories, requests for production of documents and depositions.
Electronic Discovery (ediscovery): The process of collecting, preparing, reviewing, and producing ESI in the context of the legal process.
See Discovery.
Electronic Record: Information recorded in a form that requires a computer or other machine to process it and that otherwise satisfies the definition of a record.

Electronically Stored Information (“ESI”): Any information that is created, received, maintained or stored on local workstations, laptops, central servers, personal digital assistants, cell phones, or in other electronic media.

Examples include, but are not limited to: electronic mail (“email”), calendars, word processing documents and spreadsheets, databases, videos, video files, digital images, audio files, text messages, voicemails, activity logs, etc.
ESI includes metadata.

Preservation Obligation: The obligation of agencies, managers and individual employees to ensure the preservation of documentary materials that might be or might become relevant to pending or threatened litigation.
policy_statements.target: preservation of documentary materials
conditions: that might be or might become relevant to pending or threatened litigation

policy_statements.source_text: If the documentary material was created in electronic format, it must be preserved in that original native format.
conditions: If the documentary material was created in electronic format

policy_statements.source_text: Litigation Hold: The procedure for locating and ensuring the retention of ESI subject to a preservation obligation
See Appendix A for litigation hold procedures/guidelines.

Record: All books, papers, maps, photographs, machine-readable materials, or other documentary materials, regardless of physical form or characteristics, made or received by an agency of the United States Government under Federal law or in connection with the transaction of public business and preserved or appropriate for preservation by that agency or its legitimate successor as evidence of the organization, functions, policies, decisions, procedures, operations, or other activities of the Government or because of the informational value of data in them.

Library and museum material made or acquired and preserved solely for reference or exhibition purposes, extra copies of documents preserved only for convenience of reference and stocks of publications and of processed documents are not included. (44 U.S.C. 3301)

The retention period for ESI will be consistent with Departmental and agency policies for records management or with Departmental and agency policies for maintaining and retaining data on backup media for purposes such as disaster recovery.
policy_statements.target: ESI

policy_statements.source_text: See, e.g., DR 3080-001, Records Management, and DM 3570-001, Disaster Recovery and Business Resumption Plans.
cross_references: DM 3570-001, Disaster Recovery and Business Resumption Plans

policy_statements.source_text: ESI that constitutes a "record" is subject to USDA's records management policies and to the records retention schedules that have been established for each Department agency and staff office.
policy_statements.target: ESI

policy_statements.source_text: Any ESI containing information that documents the business of the Department and is, therefore, an “agency record,” must be moved to an auditable file structure, such as an electronic file designated as containing a record series, or a paper document file in an auditable paper series, in accordance with its applicable Records Disposition Schedule.
policy_statements.target: Any ESI containing information that documents the business of the Department
conditions: in accordance with its applicable Records Disposition Schedule

policy_statements.source_text: Records not properly scheduled for disposition may not be destroyed.
policy_statements.target: Records not properly scheduled for disposition

policy_statements.source_text: Records may be destroyed only in accordance with National Archives and Records Administration (“NARA”) approved records disposition schedules.
policy_statements.target: Records
conditions: only in accordance with National Archives and Records Administration (“NARA”) approved records disposition schedules

policy_statements.source_text: A litigation hold for described documents or ESI overrides any records retention schedule or any other agency policy that may otherwise call for the transfer, disposal, or destruction of the relevant documents or ESI until the hold has been removed by the relevant Division or Field Office of the Office of the General Counsel (“OGC”), Office of Inspector General (“OIG”), or other authorized authority that ordered the hold.
policy_statements.target: any records retention schedule or any other agency policy
conditions: until the hold has been removed by the relevant Division or Field Office of the Office of the General Counsel (“OGC”), Office of Inspector General (“OIG”), or other authorized authority that ordered the hold

policy_statements.source_text: A litigation hold is generally accompanied by a records search for all responsive information.

Records searches initiated pursuant to a hold must be coordinated with agency officials, including the relevant program officials, the information technology (“IT”) staff, and the agency records officer.
policy_statements.target: Records searches initiated pursuant to a hold

policy_statements.source_text: A litigation hold should trigger notice as well to the USDA Records Officer.
policy_statements.target: USDA Records Officer

policy_statements.source_text: Each organization is responsible for notifying its subordinate activities that a hold exists or has been removed.
policy_statements.target: its subordinate activities

policy_statements.source_text: See litigation hold guidelines in Appendix A.
Many IT organizations back up email and other ESI for the purpose of restoring electronic systems in the event of disaster.
policy_statements.target: email and other ESI

policy_statements.source_text: Any decision concerning retention periods for electronic backup media should be established based upon consideration of reasonably anticipated business needs for data recovery in the event of system failure, as well as upon legal considerations such as the extent the agency or component has otherwise archived the ESI.
policy_statements.target: retention periods for electronic backup media

policy_statements.source_text: However, backup tapes are not ideally suited as a record retention mechanism because of the difficulty and expense of reconstituting them to readable format.
Thus, agencies are encouraged to seek true archiving solutions for ESI.
policy_statements.target: true archiving solutions for ESI

policy_statements.source_text: Additionally, email archived to the individual workstation should not be considered part of the institutional backup – but a part of the individual’s filing system.
policy_statements.target: email archived to the individual workstation

policy_statements.source_text: However, such individually maintained material is potentially discoverable, and therefore may be the subject of a litigation hold.

Failure to comply with this policy in preserving documents and ESI can result in unfavorable discovery orders, sanctions against the Government, disadvantage to the government's position in litigation or judgment against the Government.
It can also result in monetary or other contempt sanctions against individuals who failed to take appropriate steps to locate and segregate information subject to litigation hold.
In extreme cases, agency performance based action or disciplinary sanction may be warranted under 5 U.S.C. 4301, et seq. or 5 U.S.C. 7501, et seq.
Office of the Chief Information Officer will:
Advise on records management issues and develop Departmentwide records management policies, procedures, guidance, and training.
policy_statements.actor_name: Office of the Chief Information Officer
policy_statements.target: records management issues

policy_statements.source_text: Advise on backup media management and retention policies, procedures, guidance, and training.
policy_statements.actor_name: Office of the Chief Information Officer
policy_statements.target: backup media management and retention policies, procedures, guidance, and training

policy_statements.source_text: Work with program, OGC and OIG staff to help ensure that paper and electronic records and other non-record documentary materials, including ESI, are accessible for ediscovery purposes.
policy_statements.actor_name: Office of the Chief Information Officer
policy_statements.target: paper and electronic records and other non-record documentary materials, including ESI

policy_statements.source_text: Agency and Staff Office Heads will:
Advise on backup media management and retention policies, procedures, guidance, and training.
policy_statements.target: backup media management and retention policies, procedures, guidance, and training

policy_statements.source_text: Cooperate with OGC and OCIO in locating and preserving paper and electronic records as well as non-record ESI subject to a litigation hold.
policy_statements.target: paper and electronic records as well as non-record ESI subject to a litigation hold

policy_statements.source_text: Agency/Staff Office Records Officers will:
Develop and maintain the mission area, agency, and staff office records management program in conformance with the Department's policies and standards.
policy_statements.target: mission area, agency, and staff office records management program

policy_statements.source_text: Work with program, IT, and OGC staff to help ensure that paper and electronic records are accessible for ediscovery purposes.
policy_statements.target: paper and electronic records

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Employees will:
Maintain paper and electronic records and non-record ESI according to prescribed Department policy and procedures, including litigation holds.
policy_statements.target: paper and electronic records and non-record ESI

policy_statements.source_text: OGC will:

With regard to litigation holds initiated by OGC, work with program, IT, and Records Management staff to help ensure that paper and electronic records, as well as non-record ESI, is accessible for ediscovery purposes.
conditions: With regard to litigation holds initiated by OGC
policy_statements.target: paper and electronic records, as well as non-record ESI

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that the Departmental Records Officer is notified of all litigation hold requests and hold removals.
policy_statements.target: Departmental Records Officer

policy_statements.source_text: OIG will:

With regard to litigation holds initiated by OIG, work with program, IT, and Records Management staff to help ensure that paper and electronic records, as well as non-record ESI, is accessible for ediscovery purposes.
conditions: With regard to litigation holds initiated by OIG
policy_statements.target: paper and electronic records, as well as non-record ESI

policy_statements.target: Departmental Records Officer

Library and museum material made or acquired and preserved solely for reference or exhibition purposes, extra copies of documents preserved only for convenience of reference and stocks of publications and of processed documents are not included. (44 U.S.C. 3301)

ESI that constitutes a "record" is subject to USDA's records management policies and to the records retention schedules that have been established for each Department agency and staff office.

Any ESI containing information that documents the business of the Department and is, therefore, an “agency record,” must be moved to an auditable file structure, such as an electronic file designated as containing a record series, or a paper document file in an auditable paper series, in accordance with its applicable Records Disposition Schedule.

A litigation hold for described documents or ESI overrides any records retention schedule or any other agency policy that may otherwise call for the transfer, disposal, or destruction of the relevant documents or ESI until the hold has been removed by the relevant Division or Field Office of the Office of the General Counsel (“OGC”), Office of Inspector General (“OIG”), or other authorized authority that ordered the hold.

A litigation hold is generally accompanied by a records search for all responsive information.

Records searches initiated pursuant to a hold must be coordinated with agency officials, including the relevant program officials, the information technology (“IT”) staff, and the agency records officer.
Records searches initiated pursuant to a hold
A litigation hold should trigger notice as well to the USDA Records Officer.
Each organization is responsible for notifying its subordinate activities that a hold exists or has been removed.
See litigation hold guidelines in  Appendix A .
Many IT organizations back up email and other ESI for the purpose of restoring electronic systems in the event of disaster.

Any decision concerning retention periods for electronic backup media should be established based upon consideration of reasonably anticipated business needs for data recovery in the event of system failure, as well as upon legal considerations such as the extent the agency or component has otherwise archived the ESI.
retention periods for electronic backup media
However, backup tapes are not ideally suited as a record retention mechanism because of the difficulty and expense of reconstituting them to readable format.
Thus, agencies are encouraged to seek true archiving solutions for ESI.
Additionally, email archived to the individual workstation should not be considered part of the institutional backup – but a part of the individual’s filing system.
email archived to the individual workstation
However, such individually maintained material is potentially discoverable, and therefore may be the subject of a litigation hold.

Failure to comply with this policy in preserving documents and ESI can result in unfavorable discovery orders, sanctions against the Government, disadvantage to the government's position in litigation or judgment against the Government.
It can also result in monetary or other contempt sanctions against individuals who failed to take appropriate steps to locate and segregate information subject to litigation hold.
In extreme cases, agency performance based action or disciplinary sanction may be warranted under 5 U.S.C. 4301, *et seq.* or 5 U.S.C. 7501, *et seq
